about: The intent set — the fourth KPI set, and the only one whose queries were not written to be a test. Every query here was actually sent to search_docs while building a working @imqueue application (a car-wash fleet touching 14 of the 17 packages) on 2026-08-05, in the order it was sent, because the next line of code could not be written without the answer. See scripts/search-kpi/README.md, section 'The intent set'.
why: This is the shape of query the framework's own instructions demand and the only set that measures the cost of getting it wrong. @imqueue/mcp's instruction #1 is "Call search_docs before writing or changing @imqueue code... Never infer an API name or signature" — so an agent asks by DESCRIBING what it needs, having not yet learned the name. When that fails it does not retry; it infers, and the inference compiles. Seven of the fourteen packages in the build were wired from guesses because these queries missed, including an invented `new Logger()` and an invented `ttl` key. The other three sets cannot see this: natural is keyword autocomplete, artificial is identifiers, and question is chat-shaped phrasings written afterwards by an assistant that already knew the corpus.
rules: A query is here only if it was really sent during the build. Nothing was added, reworded or dropped afterwards, including the four that are clumsy and the three that are second attempts.

`expect` lists the reference pages that carry the answer, plus the package index page when the answer spans several symbols (JobQueue + PushOptions.delay + retry semantics, for instance). Drawn from the page inventory, never from a ranker's output.

A prose page is NOT accepted for a query that needs a signature or an option name. That exclusion is the point of the set: six reasonable tutorial sections and no signature is the failure being measured, not a partial success.
`kind` is the page type that answers — `reference` or `guide`. 17 of 19 want reference, which is where the other three sets are weakest.

`attempt` is 2 on a query that was itself a retry after the intent-shaped attempt in `retryOf` failed, and naming the package or class is what made it work. Those four pairs are the finding, not noise: discovery by name works, discovery by intent does not.

`log` records what the two rankers returned during the build. It is PROVENANCE, not a label — nothing in the harness reads it, and tuning towards it would make the metric agree with a ranker by construction.
imqueue.org only. The harness scores `!hit.external`, so a query answered on imqueue.com could not score here; none is.

`/api/faq/` is deliberately NOT accepted here, even though /api/faq/ was written from these 19 queries on 2026-08-06 and now ranks #1 for 18 of them. Accepting it would score close to 100% and retire the only measurement this project has of whether the reference page itself is reachable — which is what seven of fourteen packages were wired from guesses for. The visible cost is that micro accuracy fell about 10 points when the page shipped, because the FAQ answer takes position 1 and pushes the reference page down one slot; recall@6 did not move, which is why the floor below still holds at 100. That drop is the page working, not the ranker regressing. The question set is where /api/faq/ counts as an answer.

floor.note: recall@6 measured at ranker 05b81ad on 2026-08-06 (15 of 19), raised to 84.2 (16 of 19) the same day when BM25 length normalisation earned it — 5 queries better, 0 worse, and `expose a service method so it can be called remotely` finally crossed into the six an agent sees, from #7 to #5. RAISED AGAIN to 94.7 (18 of 19) the same day when the record-summary weight for long descriptive queries earned it: 11 better, 2 worse, and the one query with no answer anywhere in the result set — `write structured JSON logs from a service to a file` — arrived at #1. RAISED A THIRD TIME to 100 (19 of 19) when term-at-a-time BM25F plus span proximity earned it. A floor of 100 is a hair trigger by construction — one query slipping fails the build, because with 19 queries there is no slack to give — and that is deliberate: this set exists to be the consequence, and 'we lost one of the nineteen' is exactly the news it should break on. intent.js exits non-zero below this. A high-importance set with no consequence is decoration; this is the consequence. Raise it when a change earns it; lower it only deliberately, with the reason written here.
